doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Don't Blame Me and the Crazeology solo
summary: Baker praises his Don't Blame Me solo; Johnson recalls the only record with Bird and the first with a trombonist.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Do you remember the album from this same time, the one [that had] one of the most imitated solos [of yours]? I remember Slide and I learning this solo – and just about everybody else – your solo on Don’t Blame Me.
To this day I can sing the bridge on that solo.
You did a lot of playing, you know, mixing it up with mutes and things at that time, too.
Yeah, yeah. I know that I recorded Don’t Blame Me some years ago. I don’t remember that solo, no. Maybe I should learn it. Maybe I will learn it. [laughter]

It was the first time I heard somebody play consistently when you got the bridge [Baker sings from the solo] to the flat five [Baker continues to sing from the solo] and then restating the melody again.
Oh, my goodness. I wouldn’t dare attempt that today.
And also your solo, the one we were talking about on Crazeology . . .
. . . because that’s the only recording you did with Bird, I think.
To my knowledge. To my knowledge,
That’s the first time Bird had ever recorded with a trombone player.
Fact is, I’m not sure, until they did the big band things with Bill Harris, that they ever got onto that again.
